about.headline: WHO WERE THE BUCKEYES
copy: Ryan Day brought in Chip Kelly as OC in 2024 and pushed the spread to run to its full potential. {ppg|Nearly 36 a game}, elite talent at every single spot.
Then they ran the table in the playoff, beating Tennessee, Oregon, and Texas, before {record|taking down Notre Dame} 34 to 23 for the national championship.

principles.title: MOTION EVERYTHING
principles.blurb: Something moves on almost every snap, so they never see the same picture twice.
principles.detail: Our run game is built on motion and creativity, and we have got something moving on almost every single snap, so the defense never gets to line up against the same picture twice. And once we have got them chasing all that movement and worried about the run, that is what opens up everything we want to do in the pass game.

principles.title: BALL IN OUR PLAYMAKERS' HANDS
principles.blurb: Elite athletes everywhere. The whole job is getting them the ball with room to work.
principles.detail: We have got elite athletes all over the field in this offense, and the whole job of the scheme is just getting them the ball with room to work. Whether we scheme somebody open thirty yards down the field, or get our guys in space and let them go win with the ball in their hands.

principles.title: EVERYTHING HAS A COUNTER
principles.blurb: Same motion, same look, a completely different answer already installed.
principles.detail: A ton of this offense is built with a constraint play right off of it, the same motion and the same look with a completely different answer. So the second they finally take one thing away, we have already got the built-in answer sitting there installed and ready to go.

title.name: THE SPREAD TO RUN OFFENSE
title.sub: One system. Three programs. A thousand miles apart, running the same play.

teams.name: OREGON
teams.writeup: The blur years. Chip Kelly took the spread run game and strapped a jet engine to it: no huddle, no mercy. From 2009 to 2012 Oregon went 46 and 7, played for a national title, and won four straight BCS bowls out of Eugene. LaMichael James ran for over 1,700 twice while the Ducks led the country in scoring, snapping the ball before defenses could even get lined up.

teams.name: OHIO STATE
teams.writeup: The proof it still wins. Chip Kelly came back to call the plays, the spread run game set the table, and Ohio State ran through the entire sport in 2024: a national championship behind a true freshman phenom in Jeremiah Smith. Twenty years after Morgantown, the same offense is still carving defenses apart.

plays.name: Orbit Triple Option

reads.label: Read the End
reads.text: Run this option to the wide side. The whole thing starts with your orbit player coming from the slot and orbiting all the way into the backfield. It is a read option: read the read defender on the line. If he crashes down, pull it with your quarterback and get out on the perimeter.

reads.label: Pitch to the Orbit Player
reads.text: That orbit player is your pitch man, and it is what makes this one of the best triple options in the game. Get everybody swarming in on the quarterback, and the second they do, flip it out to your orbit player with a ton of room for big plays.

reads.label: Keep It
reads.text: If they overplay it to the outside, just keep it with your quarterback on the keeper.

reads.label: Hand It Off
reads.text: And if they shut the outside down completely, hand it off and get downhill with your running back. There should be big holes up the middle if they sell out to take away the edge.

adjustments: Run the option to the wide side of the field.
plays.whenToUse: This is the engine of the run game. The orbit motion gives you a true triple option with your best space weapon as the pitch man, so every way the defense plays it, you have the answer. Bait them onto the quarterback and pitch, keep it if they widen, or hand it downhill if they sell out on the edge.

plays.name: Exit RPO Read WR Screen

reads.label: Count the Numbers
reads.text: Come out with the stack to the wide side. The auto motion from the tight end fires straight out to that stack, so now you have an extra body and a numbers advantage on the perimeter. When you have the numbers, flip it out to the screen.

reads.label: Screen to the Perimeter
reads.text: With multiple blockers out in front, you are getting the ball into one of your best players' hands on the edge. You can pick up massive gains out on the perimeter with this.

reads.label: Hand It Up the Middle
reads.text: If they adjust and widen out to take the screen away, just hand the ball off up the middle. They have emptied the box to deal with the perimeter, so now you have the numbers inside and can get downhill.

adjustments: Come out with the stack to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: This is the very first thing you install. It is a built-in numbers read: get the extra body to the perimeter with the tight end motion, and take whatever the defense gives you. They stay inside, you throw the screen. They widen out, you hand it downhill. There is no wrong answer.

plays.name: QB Zone

reads.label: Box Count
reads.text: In empty, the defense respects the pass and keeps two safeties deep, leaving only four defenders in the box against six blockers (five OL plus the QB). Run the zone when you have that numbers advantage.

reads.label: Run Lane
reads.text: Default run path is between guard-tackle or tackle-guard. Look for the crease off the double teams climbing to the second level.

reads.label: Bounce Read
reads.text: If the defense pinches inside and collapses the interior gaps, the zone bounces to the outside where a receiver sets the edge block.

reads.label: Pass Opener
reads.text: If the defense starts aggressively collapsing on the QB zone, the outside passing lanes open up, so trigger your empty passing options.

adjustments: Bounce outside when the interior pinches.
Receiver sets the edge block.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when they are in a two-high shell out of respect for your empty sets. You have six on four in the box, that is free yards. Run it, make them pay for sitting back, and when they crash down to stop it, you have already set up the pass.

plays.name: RPO Counter Bubble

reads.label: Numbers on the Bubble
reads.text: Come out with your bubble to the wide side. If you have a numbers advantage out there pre-snap, drop it out to the bubble as soon as you snap it. You have a one-on-one block on the outside and room to operate, so let your dynamic receiver go make plays.

reads.label: Read the Overhang
reads.text: Same thing at the snap: if you see the player over the top of the bubble crash down on the run, drop it out there and let him go to work.

reads.label: Hand Off the Counter
reads.text: When you hand it off is when you do not have the numbers advantage and they stay over the top of your bubble. Now you have a nice pull action coming across the formation, with your guard and backside tight end pulling all the way across for two lead blockers to gain big yards on the ground.

adjustments: Come out with the bubble to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: This is a numbers read off the counter run. If they leave the perimeter light, throw the bubble and let your playmaker work one-on-one. If they cover it and load up over the top, hand it off behind the guard and tight end pulling across for two lead blockers downhill.

plays.name: Sprint Out Screen

reads.label: The Corner off the Back
reads.text: This is an auto rollout, so you are out on the perimeter right away with a nice flood action. Your first read is that corner route from the back. If the flat defender stays shallow, fire it in there as the back breaks to the corner.

reads.label: Drop It in the Flat
reads.text: If you start rolling out and see them playing way off, just drop it down in the flat right away and let your slot receiver make plays in the open field.

reads.label: Backside Tight End Screen
reads.text: The best part of this play is the tight end screen on the backside. As you roll out, the whole flow of the defense comes with you to the other side of the field, and the second you drop it to that tight end there is a ton of room for him to work in space with blockers in front.

adjustments: Come out with the slot receiver to the wide side.
Slide the protection to the side you are rolling out to.
plays.whenToUse: Run this one stock. It is an auto rollout that puts you on the perimeter with a flood in front of you and a backside tight end screen as the home run. Take the corner if the flat sits, the flat if they play off, and if the defense chases the rollout, come all the way back to that screen.

plays.name: Curl Flat

reads.label: Seam vs Cover 3
reads.text: This is a one-play touchdown against Cover 3. Your slot breaks it inside and then takes off up the far seam. The comeback holds the backside defender and the tight end holds the safety in the middle, so against Cover 3 you can bomb it over the top for a score.

reads.label: Split It vs Cover 2
reads.text: Against Cover 2, if their linebackers stay shallow, you have two vertical routes splitting the field. Go to whichever one is more open, and once the safeties get pulled outside, fire it in.

reads.label: Answers vs Man
reads.text: For your checkdowns and answers against man, you have the comeback working the sideline and the dig over the middle. Both are good options versus man coverage.

reads.label: Chip and Release
reads.text: Your chip and release running back is sitting in the flat as the checkdown if everything else is covered.

adjustments: Come out with the trips to the wide side.
Wide-side tight end on a streak.
Backside outside receiver on a comeback.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you need a shot that has an answer for every coverage. It is a one-play touchdown against Cover 3, it splits Cover 2 down the field, and it has the comeback, dig, and flat checkdown built in against man. Set it up with the streak and the comeback and let the slot go win over the top.

plays.name: PA Y Cross

reads.label: Tight End Crosser
reads.text: Primary read on all downs. If the flat defender bites down on the running back fake and the linebackers stay in the middle, fire the tight end crosser coming across the field. Works vs both man and zone.

reads.label: Post Sit
reads.text: If the crosser is taken away or the flat is sitting too far back, look for the post sit route to settle down in front of the deep defenders. As linebackers chase the crosser, the post sit finds the hole behind them.

reads.label: Whip Route
reads.text: Third option. If defenders are dropping back underneath the crosser and post sit, wait for the whip receiver to plant and break back outside, then fire it in. Solid vs zone, still viable vs man.

reads.label: Running Back Flat
reads.text: Final checkdown after the play action fake. If quick pressure is coming or everyone is sitting in coverage, dump it to the running back leaking into the flat.

adjustments: Come out with the stack to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: This is your bread and butter play action concept, run it when you need a reliable chunk play against any coverage. Stack to the wide side, sell the fake, and let the crosser do the work. If they take it away, you have answers underneath and over the top.

plays.name: Exit HB Crossscreen

reads.label: Outside Screen (Numbers Advantage)
reads.text: At the snap, count defenders vs blockers on the outside screen. If you outnumber them, two blockers and a ball carrier against two or fewer defenders, throw the receiver screen immediately.

reads.label: Linebacker Overhang Check
reads.text: Even if the numbers look even, check if a linebacker is overhanging or shading to the outside. If so, the numbers advantage is negated, so hold the ball and let the RB cross.

reads.label: RB Crossscreen (Default)
reads.text: If no clear numbers advantage exists on the outside, hold the ball, let the running back cross the formation, and drop it down to him with blockers out in front.

reads.label: Red Zone Adjustment
reads.text: In the red zone, flow defenders tend to stay inside. Count the numbers at the snap. If the ball carrier outnumbers the edge defenders, go outside to the receiver screen for a score.

adjustments: Stack the trips to the wide side.
RB crosses the opposite direction.
Receiver screen on the perimeter.
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want a built-in either-or screen concept that attacks both sides of the field. Stack the trips wide, let the defense show you the numbers at the snap, and take what they give you. It is a money call in the red zone when defenders collapse inside and the perimeter opens right up.

plays.name: Exit PA FK Screen Wheel ZONE

reads.label: Wheel (Back Shoulder)
reads.text: Primary read is the tight end wheeling upfield off the exit motion. The stack receiver on a streak or post pulls the deep blue defender back, clearing space behind him. Back shoulder the wheel along the sideline, away from the deep blue defender, for a big gain.

reads.label: Crosser
reads.text: If the wheel isn't there, look to the crosser coming across the middle. If linebackers are biting down and the deep blue defenders are occupied, drop it in over the linebacker's head, in front of the safety, as the receiver breaks across the field.

reads.label: Option Route (RB)
reads.text: If everyone is dropping back in zone coverage or users are chasing the crosser, dump it to the running back on the option route. He'll sit down versus zone or break in or out versus man.

adjustments: Stack to the short side.
Front of stack receiver on a streak or post stem.
Solo backside receiver on a streak.
RB on an option route.
plays.whenToUse: Run this when they are giving you zone all game. Stack the trips to the short side, let the exit motion do the work, and drop that wheel in behind the deep blues. They can't guard it. You have three answers built in, wheel, crosser, or option route, so there is no bad look.

plays.name: Exit PA FK Screen Wheel MAN

reads.label: The Wheel vs Man
reads.text: This is a designed man beater, and there is man coverage all over the game right now. Your go-to is that auto motion tight end, the exact same motion as Exit RPO Read WR Screen. He fires out to the stack and against man his defender ends up in trail. When he wheels in behind the stack, either he already has separation or you catch a natural pick right in the middle. Either way he comes wide open on that wheel for huge plays down the field.

reads.label: The Slant
reads.text: If the wheel isn't there after the snap, you have the slant from your back of stack receiver. He is really tough to press off that stack, he breaks it inside, and that is a lot of easy yards.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: You also have the shallow cross from your solo receiver working the shallow middle of the field as another option underneath.

reads.label: The Deep Post
reads.text: And the last really good one: if they bring their safeties down and start playing everything shallow, you have the deep post attacking right over the top. Get aggressive on the underneath stuff and you go hit them deep.

adjustments: Come out with the stack to the wide side.
Back of stack receiver on a slant.
Block the running back.
plays.whenToUse: This is the man-beater version. Stack to the wide side and let the exit-motion tight end wheel in behind the stack against man, where his defender gets stuck in trail or you catch a natural pick. If the wheel is covered, you have the slant, the shallow cross, and the deep post all built in.

plays.name: Corner Strike

reads.label: C Route (Outside Break)
reads.text: Primary read vs man coverage. Sharp out-breaking route along the sideline, throw on the break and drop it over the top for the toe tap. If separation isn't great, purposely under-throw it and let the receiver come back to the ball, using his body to squeeze the defender away.

reads.label: Option Route (Slot)
reads.text: If there is safety help over the top, especially single high, the slot runs a dig across the field. If there is no safety help or a zero blitz is coming, he converts to a post, so take him over the top with the bomb.

reads.label: Slant (Motioned In)
reads.text: Motion the backside outside receiver in before the snap. The motion forces an outside shade and creates better separation as he breaks across. Can be held and thrown as a deep crosser or shallow cross if the receiver gets across the entire formation.

reads.label: Check-Down to Chips (vs Zone)
reads.text: If the defense zones off and coverage is deep across the board, the chip-and-release tight ends will secure the edges and release into the flat. Check it down to either tight end.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
Backside receiver on a slant, motion in.
plays.whenToUse: Call this against man coverage, that is what it is built for. You still get the empty spacing advantages, but those chip tight ends give you built-in blitz protection. If they bring zero man, you have answers. If they drop into zone, you have the flats. This play handles it all.

plays.name: Orbit PA Cross

reads.label: Y Cross
reads.text: Look to the tight end crosser first. If the flat defender stays too shallow respecting the orbit swing, drop the crosser in over his head at about 20 yards.

reads.label: Post Sit
reads.text: If the user linebacker is playing underneath the crosser, move to the post sit on the backside. Throw on the break, as soon as he starts to sit, fire the ball. Click on and attack the football, don't let the DB drive on it.

reads.label: Post Sit vs Zone
reads.text: Against zone, flat defenders widen to respect the swing and linebackers sit underneath the crosser, opening a throwing lane for the post sit as he settles in the zone. Drive it in there.

reads.label: Checkdown (Swing Passes)
reads.text: If defenders are dropping deep or pressure is coming, go to either the orbit motion swing to the short side or the running back swing to the wide side. Get the ball in space and let them work.

adjustments: Come out with the tight end to the wide side.
Orbit motion swing to the short side.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you have been running orbit all game and defenses are overplaying the run. The more success you have with those orbit runs, the more deadly this play action becomes. If they are run committing or bringing a big blitz off the orbit motion, this is exactly when you hit them with the cross or post sit over the top.

plays.name: Orbit PA Y Corner

reads.label: The Corner Route
reads.text: This is built off the orbit motion, so it looks absolutely identical to Orbit Triple Option. A hard play action fake pulls the linebackers and the user down to stop the run. Your first read is the corner route from the tight end. If he gets behind the flat defenders, drop it in over the top. It is a really good option against man too.

reads.label: The Dig
reads.text: Once you have sucked the linebackers and the user down on the play action fake, the dig attacks the middle of the field. That is also where you go if the user or linebackers leave to help on the corner route.

reads.label: Checkdown to the Flat
reads.text: Last one, for a checkdown: if everybody is playing way back, your orbit player is out in the flat. Drop it off to him and let him make plays in the open field.

adjustments: Come out with the tight end to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: This is the counter to Orbit Triple Option, and it looks exactly the same pre-snap. Run it once you have them chasing the orbit run. They bite on the fake, you hit the corner over the top or the dig underneath. Run it stock and let the identical picture do the work.

plays.name: Fade Smash

reads.label: 1st Read - Slot Fade
reads.text: Primary read on every snap. Against Cover 2, the slot fade gets behind the corner as he sinks to the flat, throw it back shoulder along the sideline as soon as the receiver clears him. Against Cover 3, wait for the deep blue defender to get pulled by the streak, then drop it in behind him on the back shoulder.

reads.label: 2nd Read - TE Option Route
reads.text: Against single-high Cover 3, if the flat defender rides the slot fade hard, bring eyes to the tight end running a skinny post down the seam. The backside post holds the safety and the TE splits the seam, so fire it in. Against two-high, the TE breaks hard across the formation on a post as the deep defender gets run off, drop it in as he breaks.

reads.label: 3rd Read - Wide Side Post
reads.text: Against man coverage or when the slot fade and TE routes aren't there, work to the wide receiver's post breaking over the middle. Three vertical routes clear out defenders and the post finds the window between safeties with the linebackers staying shallow.

reads.label: Checkdown - RB Option Route
reads.text: If everyone drops into coverage underneath the verticals, the running back sits down in zone or breaks in or out to the sideline vs man. Gets very good separation versus man. Use as a safe outlet on third and medium or when nothing else develops.

adjustments: Short-side X receiver on a streak.
Wide-side X receiver on a post.
Tight end aligned to the wide side.
RB on an option route.
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want to stress every level of the defense with one play. It beats Cover 2 with the back-shoulder slot fade, rips Cover 3 on the seam, and the post cleans up vs man. Call it when you need a big play and want options at every level.

plays.name: Orbit RPO Peek Y Pop

reads.label: 1st Read - Off-Ball Linebacker
reads.text: Watch the off-ball linebacker on the side of the peak pop. If he fires down on the play fake or the orbit, the peak pop window opens up.

reads.label: 2nd Read - Safety or Nickel Over Top
reads.text: Once the linebacker bites, check if the safety or nickel is capping the tight end on the peak route. If he widens or stays back, throw the peak pop, it is a money route.

reads.label: 3rd Read - Hand Off
reads.text: If the linebacker stays home and the safety or nickel caps the pop pass, take the run. The orbit motion helps widen defenders and creates a large running lane downhill.

reads.label: 4th Read - Orbit Player
reads.text: If both the peak pop and the run are taken away, the orbit player is available as a quick throw to the flat. Limited YAC potential, but salvages 4 to 5 yards if needed.

adjustments: Tight end motions to the wide side.
Orbit player starts the short side.
plays.whenToUse: Red zone is where I love this most, linebackers bite and that peak pops open every time. But don't sleep on it on third down either. Any time you need a chunk play and want to stress multiple levels at once, this is your call.

plays.name: RPO Alert Power

reads.label: Numbers Advantage Pre-Snap
reads.text: Scan the perimeter defenders at the snap. If there are two defenders against your screen side and they are backpedaling or giving cushion, you have the numbers advantage, so throw the screen.

reads.label: Post-Snap Defender Reaction
reads.text: If a defender who was counted pre-snap dives down into the run fit on the snap, the numbers flip in your favor outside, fire the screen immediately.

reads.label: No Numbers Advantage
reads.text: If there is no numbers advantage pre-snap and defenders are not backing off post-snap, hand the ball off and run the power.

reads.label: Backside Glance
reads.text: A backside glance route exists but the timing is inconsistent, so treat it as a non-factor. Keep your eyes on the perimeter numbers read only.

adjustments: Puller kicks across the formation.
Screen to the perimeter numbers side.
plays.whenToUse: Run this in any situation where you want to stress the defense horizontally off power. It is a two-option RPO, screen or hand off. Perfect for short yardage when they load the box, and deadly against teams that like to blitz or crash defenders down. If they give you the numbers outside, take it every time.

plays.name: Shot HB Wheel

reads.label: The Back out of the Backfield
reads.text: Come out with your running back to the short side. The go-to route is that back out of the backfield, and as soon as you snap it that is where you are looking. If the flat defender and everybody is playing back at the snap, just get it to him quick as soon as he cuts up field.

reads.label: Climb the Wheel
reads.text: If the flat is playing a little shallower, wait for your back to climb up in behind him. The streak is running the deep defender off, so the second your back crosses in behind that flat defender's head, drop it in there and he has a ton of open room for big plays.

reads.label: The Deep Crosser
reads.text: You have got two crossers on this play. If the running back is ever taken away, the deep crosser is attacking the other side of the field. So if the linebackers or the user react to that back, you go right to that crosser.

reads.label: The Tight End Underneath
reads.text: Your underneath option is the tight end, and this one is really good against man. Go to him if that flat defender turns and runs with the wheel, or if they are just playing way deep underneath your running back. That shallow cross comes through to the short side of the field and you drop the ball right into him.

adjustments: Come out with the running back to the short side.
Short-side outside receiver on a streak.
plays.whenToUse: This is a star play that turns your running back into a home run threat, and it has an answer at every level. Take the quick throw if everyone is sitting back, or let the wheel climb behind a shallow flat defender with the streak clearing the deep man out. If they take the back away you go to the deep crosser, and the tight end shallow is sitting there underneath as your man beater.
